t: After the 1954 Geneva Conference divided Vietnam at the 17th parallel, the State of Vietnam ruled the South, and in October 1955 a referendum widely marred by fraud deposed Bảo Đại and made Ngô Đình Diệm president of the new republic.

Diệm's authoritarian rule under the doctrine of Personalism ended in the Buddhist crisis and his killing in a US-backed coup in 1963; after four years of military juntas, the 1967 constitution opened the Second Republic under Nguyễn Văn Thiệu.

At the Paris Peace Accords of 1973 South Vietnam fielded about one and one-half million troops, but after US forces withdrew and aid was cut, the North's conventional invasion of 1975 ended with Dương Văn Minh's unconditional surrender on 30 April.
dyk: In the referendum of 1955 that made Diệm president, over 380,000 more votes were cast than there were registered voters, and in Saigon he was credited with 133% of the vote; his American advisers had recommended a more modest margin of 60 to 70 percent.
ev: Ngô Đình Diệm's referendum removes Bảo Đại as head of state, and on 26 October Diệm declares himself president of the Republic of Vietnam
The Huế Phật Đản shootings of 8 May set off the Buddhist crisis, and on 1 November Diệm is overthrown and killed in a coup led by General Dương Văn Minh
A new constitution creates a bicameral legislature, and Nguyễn Văn Thiệu is elected president with 34% of the vote in a widely criticised poll
The People's Army of Vietnam and the Việt Cộng launch the Tet Offensive, which fails militarily but marks a turning point in US support
The government begins the Land-to-the-Tiller program of land reform, limiting individual landholdings to 15 hectares
The Paris Peace Accords are signed on 27 January, and US military forces leave South Vietnam at the end of March
Thiệu announces that the war has restarted, and China attacks South Vietnamese forces in the Paracel Islands and takes control of them
Communist forces overrun Saigon, and President Dương Văn Minh surrenders South Vietnam unconditionally on 30 April

f.founder: Ngô Đình Diệm, who declared himself president on 26 October 1955 after the referendum of 23 October
f.predecessor: State of Vietnam (1949–1955), an associated state within the French Union under Bảo Đại
f.successor: Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam (1975), merged into the Socialist Republic of Vietnam on 2 July 1976
